ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the quadrilateral $\mathrm{ABCD}, \mathrm{AD}=\mathrm{BC}, \angle \mathrm{DAC}=50^{\circ}$, $\angle \mathrm{DCA}=65^{\circ}$ and $\angle \mathrm{ACB}=70^{\circ}$. How big is $\angle \mathrm{ABC}$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is quadrilateral ABCD, A is above, C is below, and AC is the diagonal connecting A and C. The figure marks ∠DAC = 50°, ∠DCA = 65°, ∠ACB = 70°, and gives AD = BC. Then reason: In triangle ACD, ∠ADC = 180° − 50° − 65° = 65°. Therefore ∠ADC = ∠DCA, so the sides opposite these two angles are equal, obtaining AC = AD. Also because it is known that AD = BC, so AC = BC. Thus triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle with AC and BC as the legs, the vertex angle ∠ACB = 70°, so the base angles are equal: ∠ABC = (180° − 70°) / 2 = 55°.

method.method_draft: Use direct angle chasing with isosceles triangles. From the image/text, identify diagonal AC splitting quadrilateral ABCD into triangles ACD and ABC, with ∠DAC = 50°, ∠DCA = 65°, ∠ACB = 70°, and AD = BC. In triangle ACD, compute ∠ADC = 180° − 50° − 65° = 65°. Since ∠ADC = ∠DCA, the opposite sides are equal, so AC = AD. Combine this with the given AD = BC to get AC = BC. Thus triangle ABC is isosceles with vertex angle ∠ACB = 70°, so its base angles at A and B are equal: ∠ABC = (180° − 70°)/2 = 55°.

method.method_draft: Use side-ratio computation via the sine rule. From the text/image, in triangle ACD we know ∠DAC = 50° and ∠DCA = 65°, so ∠ADC = 65°. By the sine rule in triangle ACD, AD/AC = sin(65°)/sin(65°) = 1, hence AD = AC. Since the text gives AD = BC, conclude BC = AC. Now let x = ∠ABC in triangle ABC. Since ∠ACB = 70°, the remaining angle is ∠BAC = 110° − x. Apply the sine rule in triangle ABC: BC/AC = sin(∠BAC)/sin(∠ABC) = sin(110° − x)/sin x. Because BC/AC = 1, we get sin(110° − x) = sin x. The valid triangle-angle solution is 110° − x = x, so x = 55°. Therefore ∠ABC = 55°.
